scenario: Hierarchical error-code prefix matching per LCCO.8.3.2 — `auth` matches `auth.failed` and `auth.expired`; `auth.failed` matches only `auth.failed`. A rule with an `error` clause (bare, matching any code) compiles cleanly. Full prefix-pattern matching syntax (`error ["auth.*"]:`) is exercised by the engine; compile-level pin is that the error clause itself is legal.
rules_ds:
schema SvcActionReply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    status: Int

service svc.action:
    kwarg entity_id: String
    response SvcActionReply

schema Trig scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    call svc.action entity_id: t.entity_id cooldown: 1_min
        on response.status == 200:
            log info "ok"
        error:
            log info "any error caught"
